messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing steady queue growth and p99 latency spikes when traffic hits redwood-large-v1 in us-west-2 during peak today. A bunch of requests are getting 429s or long tails. Thinking we should add automatic spillover to compatible variants when the primary is saturated instead of returning errors. Thoughts?

devon: +1 we need something that doesn't require manual route changes during incidents. 

sam: Agree. Two quick questions: how do we define "saturated"? GPU mem full, request queue length, or tokens/sec? Need a concrete signal.

maya: Good call. I was thinking a hybrid signal: queue depth > 500 OR sustained GPU util > 90% for 30s OR backend error rate > 1%. That should avoid flapping from transient blips.

iris: We also need to consider quality regressions when switching variants. Can't silently send to a cheaper quantized model without tracking eval metrics.

luis: For the telemetry side, we should emit events like: routing.spillover.trigger, routing.variant_selected, routing.spillover.recover. Attach metadata: route_id, customer_tier, primary_model, selected_variant, reason_code, origin_region. That lets console/team graphs break down by customer tier.

anya: Console UX: add a per-route toggle for "enable spillover on capacity" + a small cost/latency estimate showing avg token cost change and expected latency delta. Also a metric card showing current spillover rate (1m/5m) and a sparklines.

sam: API semantics: clients might want to know when they were served by a non-primary variant. I propose we set response headers: X-Model-Variant and X-Model-Routing-Reason (e.g., primary_saturation). Also include a boolean in the SDK response: metadata.variant.

devon: Implementation approach: keep routing decision in the control plane so it's observable and consistent across hosts. Hosts should advertise real-time capacity signals via our capacity topic. Routing should pick a candidate variant atomically per request.

maya: Example route config (draft):
```
route: embeddings-prod-usw2
  primary_model: redwood-large-v1
  spillover_policy:
    mode: capacity
    threshold_pct: 90            # triggers when primary util >= 90%
    hold_for_seconds: 30         # avoid rapid oscillation
    candidates:
      - redwood-large-quant
      - redwood-medium-v2
    selection_strategy: deterministic_priority # or probabilistic_weighted
```

luis: For selection_strategy we might want probabilistic_weighted to avoid thundering herd on a single variant. e.g., give redwood-large-quant 70% of overflow and redwood-medium-v2 30% depending on cost/quality tradeoffs.

iris: We should couple this with quality monitoring: sample 1% of requests that get spilled and run quick evals or reruns against the primary in the background to catch regressions. If quality drift exceeds threshold, auto-disable spillover for that customer or route.

anya: Rollout plan: feature flag + console toggle. Start on internal routes, then 1% of external traffic, monitor: spillover_rate, latency_p99, cost_per_1k_tokens, quality_regression_score. Increase to 10% if stable.

sam: Alerting rules: page if spillover_rate > 5% for > 10m for Tier 1 customers, or if spillover_cost_delta > 20% unexpectedly. Also SLO health: if primary p99 > target for >5m AND spillover didn't reduce errors, escalate.

devon: Edge cases: what if candidate variants are also saturated? We should have a graceful degrade path: 1) try next candidate, 2) if none available, optionally queue with soft timeout or return 503 with hint to backoff. Also record that fallback chain in telemetry.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] scheduled rollout job created: spillover-capacity-gate v1 -> canary cluster at 23:40 UTC; config stored at infra/routes/spillover/v1.yaml

maya: Nice. One more policy decision: per-customer tier behavior. For enterprise customers we might prefer to never slip them to quantized variants unless explicitly allowed in contract. For freemium tier send to cheaper variants aggressively. So routing decision needs customer_tier as input.

luis: Add tier to routing key and to metrics. Metric examples we should add to dashboards: 
- routing.spillover.rate (by route, by tier)
- routing.spillover.latency_delta (p50/p95/p99)
- routing.spillover.cost_delta (per 1k tokens)
- routing.spillover.quality_regression_pct
- routing.spillover.repeat_count (how often same request spills multiple times)

anya: Console should surface a per-customer timeline where you can see when they were spilled and which variant served them. For enterprise, show consent/allowed_variants flag.

sam: We need to decide whether to allow admins to set per-route candidate lists or to auto-generate compatible candidates. Auto-generate is convenient but risky. Maybe default to auto-recommended candidates with explicit opt-in for production routes.

maya: Proposed next steps: 1) RFC PR describing signals, config, and telemetry schema; 2) small prototype that implements control-plane decision + host capacity publish; 3) console mockups for toggle and cards; 4) rollout via feature flag with canary and sampling checks. I'll open the RFC and prototype tickets.

devon: I'll help with the control-plane part. Agree on the metric names and events.

iris: I'll draft the sampling/quality harness and suggested thresholds for automatic disable.

luis: I'll add backend telemetry fields and a Grafana dashboard template.

maya: Thanks — will follow up in the RFC. If anyone has constraints (legal/contract) re: variant switching for certain customers, ping me here so we can bake that into the tier rules. :party-popper:
